newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks to firm but gains seen limited.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks to firm but gains seen limited.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to firm on Thursday with the Nikkei average eyeing the closing high for the year near 20,500, brokers said. But they said profit-taking pressure was intense above that barrier and gains were likely to be limited.
On Wednesday, the 225-share Nikkei surged 461.45 points or 2.32 percent to finish at 20,351.34. Its June futures added 540 points to end at 20,400.
"Exporters led by high-techs, telecommunications, cable and wire shares have been rising and should continue to provide support," a dealer at a foreign brokerage said.
Brokers said, however, that rather than the rises in the indices, market attention was on turnover, which has been rather thin lately.
"In order to generate solid gains, turnover needs to grow to about 500 million shares," said Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager.
On Wednesday, only 374 million issues changed hands despite the jump in the Nikkei average.
"Rather than rises in the indices, market attention is on turnover volume," he added.

Some high-tech issues, especially laggards, continued to rally from the previous day, with Advantest Corp and Tokyo Electron Ltd jumping briefly to new highs for the calendar year. Advantest added 400 yen to 7,630 and Tokyo Electron gained 370 yen to 5,590.

Banks powered higher late in the morning, amid speculation that hedge funds were buyers of the shares. Sakura Bank Ltd rose 14 yen to 730, the second most heavily traded issue on the Tokyo bourse with turnover of 3.17 million shares.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd rose 40 yen to 1,440 in trade totalling 2.97 million shares.
Banks, trading houses, electrical equipment, iron/steel and chemicals were at the top of the list of gaining sectors.
Miscellaneous manufacturers, air transport, fisheries, ship building and non-ferrous metals headed the list of retreaters.

Bandai Co Ltd continued to slump following the recent cancellation of its planned merger with Sega Enterprises Ltd. Toymaker Bandai lost 110 yen to 2,560 and Sega, a video-game machine producer, fell 10 yen to 3,770.
Brokers said that the market would be keeping an eye on Japan's industrial output data for April and forecasts for May and June, due out at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT).

"If the forecasts are bullish, it could give investors confidence about the future of the economy, which is supportive for stocks," one broker said. "Strong data, however, could move other markets and thus have a negative effect on stocks. It is difficult to predict what will happen."
Previously, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry said output in the April-June quarter was expected to fall 0.4 percent from the previous quarter.
The TOPIX index added 2.25 points or 0.15 percent to reach 1,505.50. The Nikkei 300 rose 0.26 point or 0.09 percent to 291.22.
